correctness.rationale: The class-size exponent is the rank of y↦xy−yx since (1+x)(1+y)=(1+y)(1+x) exactly when xy=yx. A triple bracket has leading term γ₀ for n≥4 and γ₀−γ₂ for n=3, so the class is three in every characteristic. At a=0 the two parity blocks share the determinant condition and each is nonzero when b≠0. Single-parity nonzero support of a gives ranks (2,2) for A,B and no residual rank because L preserves parity. Adjacent nonzero support gives ranks (3,3): up to rotation, for support {0,1}, the B equations force v₁=v₂=v₃=0; for {0,1,2}, they force v₂=v₃=0 and one relation on v₀,v₁; on full support each vᵢ/(aᵢaᵢ₊₁) is the same. Then L(a)=−B(b) puts the image of ker A in im B. Multiplying pair counts by q⁴ and dividing by the corresponding class size reproduces the displayed polynomial, including its total at T=1. The length-two witnesses give proportional output forms at n=3 and three independent forms at every n≥5. Independent replay, python3 /workspace/frozen_math_replay.py 4, exhausts all 65,536 coefficient pairs over GF(4) by literal path multiplication and obtains ranks 0,2,4,6 with counts 1,75,7860,57600; it supplements, not replaces, the characteristic-free argument.

value.rationale: The four-cycle is a natural exception within a uniform truncated path-algebra family: parity blocks explain exactly why odd ranks disappear only there. The explicit ordinary conjugacy distribution combines a usable invariant over every finite field with a sharp family boundary, rather than tabulating an isolated small example.
residual_risks: For n≠4 this proves existence of an odd rank, not a full size distribution.
